State Transition Table

Source: R/plot-transition.R
transition_table.Rd

The transition counts behind the flow and network views, as a tidy data frame. By default every consecutive move is aggregated over time (the numbers transition_plot() draws); by_time = TRUE instead returns one block per consecutive time pair, matching the alluvial flow_plot().

Usage

transition_table(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'vasstra_sequences'
transition_table(x, by_time = FALSE, ...)

# S3 method for class 'vasstra_trajectories'
transition_table(x, by_time = FALSE, group = NULL, ...)

# S3 method for class 'vasstra'
transition_table(x, ...)

Arguments

x

A vasstra_sequences, vasstra_trajectories, or vasstra object.

...

Not used.

by_time

Return per-time-step transitions (TRUE) or the time-aggregated table (FALSE, default).

group

Optional trajectory label restricting the table to one trajectory's subjects.

Value

A tidy data frame. Aggregated: from, to, count, and probability (row-normalized within from). With by_time = TRUE, also from_time and to_time, with probability normalized within each (from_time, from).

See also

transition_plot() and flow_plot() to draw these movements, transition_centrality() for network centralities.

Examples

data("engagement", package = "VaSSTra")
fit <- vasstra(engagement, n_states = 3, n_trajectories = 3)
transition_table(fit)
#>      from      to count probability
#> 1 State 1 State 1   156 0.666666667
#> 2 State 2 State 1    73 0.152083333
#> 3 State 3 State 1     2 0.007142857
#> 4 State 1 State 2    73 0.311965812
#> 5 State 2 State 2   335 0.697916667
#> 6 State 3 State 2    73 0.260714286
#> 7 State 1 State 3     5 0.021367521
#> 8 State 2 State 3    72 0.150000000
#> 9 State 3 State 3   205 0.732142857
transition_table(fit, by_time = TRUE)
#>    from_time to_time    from      to count probability
